{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Kubient / AP)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of Exhibit 10.14 Master Services Agreement, dated 5 February  
**Party posture:** We act for the Customer (AP).

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 19 playbook rules. The commercial architecture is favourable to us: this is a non-exclusive revenue-share arrangement in which Kubient pays us, with no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no non-solicit, no liquidated damages or termination penalty, and no audit right running against us. Vendor indemnification (Section 10(a)), the performance warranty (Section 9(b)), assignment (paragraph (h)), termination for convenience and governing law/venue (Section 14(a), Delaware law / New York courts) are all compliant, several of them at the playbook fallback.

Five items require action. Three are omissions — no IP/data ownership article, no insurance covenant, and no post-termination transition or data-return obligation — and two are deviations: Section 7 contains no monetary liability cap at all, and the only post-Initial-Term exit requires 90 days' notice, exceeding our 60-day fallback ceiling. Of these, the absence of insurance, the at-will revocability of the licence grant, and the bare "return **or destroy**" treatment of our data on termination sit in walk-away territory and are our priority asks.

Two proposed redlines did not pass verification (IP ownership and licence grant) and need manual drafting before we send comments.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 10(a), 9(b), 11; Section 7 carve-out) | Broad Kubient defend-and-indemnify covering IP, law and data security; procedure standard. Our reciprocal indemnity is marginally wide but does not shift Services risk to us. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment / change of control | Compliant (fallback) | Preamble (paragraph (h); termination provisions p0016) | Mutual affiliate/successor carve-out; no change-of-control trigger or re-pricing right. No competitor bar or notice mechanic — noted only. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) | Expressly non-exclusive; our freedom to use other agents preserved. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | Preamble (paragraphs 4(a), 5, 7(a)) | No Customer-payable liquidated sum; notice-period fees are earned revenue share. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1; p0002, p0041, p0044) | No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use covenant on us. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (fallback) | Preamble (Section 5; Initial Term / notice provisions) | 90 days' notice each way, no penalty; suspension during a 1-year Initial Term is acceptable. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 5, 6(a)) | No audit, inspection or system-access right against us; better than preferred. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | Preamble (Sections 14(a), 8) | Delaware law (fallback) with exclusive New York courts (preferred). Law/forum split and the Section 8 arbitration tension are drafting tidy-ups only. |
| Medium | **IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data** | **Missing** | Preamble (Section 6(a) p0025; Section 14(b) p0065; warranties p0039–p0040) | No ownership or data article; nothing confirms we retain rights in our Content, Properties, Requests and data, or addresses deliverables. No assignment of our IP, so not walk-away. **Proposed redline failed verification.** |
| Medium | **LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability** | **Deviation** | Preamble (Sections 7, 5) | Only a mutual consequential-damages exclusion; no monetary cap, so direct liability is unlimited both ways — fails the 12-month fallback. Redline repaired. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 1, 5) | No MFN or best-terms obligation on us. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Compliant | Preamble (Section 5 p0023; Section 1 p0001; p0014, p0062) | Pure revenue share, no minimum spend, volume or true-up. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant | Preamble (p0061, p0066, p0051–p0052, p0070) | No non-solicit binding us. |
| Medium | **RENEWAL — Auto-renewal / notice window** | **Deviation** | Preamble (Initial Term and renewal provisions) | 1-year renewals acceptable, but the only exit requires 90 days' notice, exceeding the 60-day fallback ceiling. No renewal uplift language today. Redline repaired. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Compliant | Preamble (Section 9(b) p0034–p0041; Section 13 disclaimer) | Ongoing Term-long warranty; disclaimer expressly excepts the express warranties; no exclusive-remedy limitation. |
| Low | **INSURANCE — Vendor insurance** | **Missing** | Preamble (p0000–p0074; new subsection (j) after p0073) | No insurance covenant of any kind despite Kubient handling visitor data (p0035) and our Confidential Information (Section 12) — walk-away territory. Redline repaired. |
| Low | **LICENSE — Licence grant scope** | **Deviation** | Preamble (paragraph 2; paragraphs 4, 21; p0072) | Grant runs to "Customer" only, with no affiliates/contractors, and is expressly "revocable" without qualification — at-will revocation is walk-away territory. **Proposed redline failed verification.** |
| Low | **TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return** | **Missing** | Preamble (Section 4(c)) | No transition assistance and no obligation to return or export our Content, Requests or data; "return **or destroy**" leaves Kubient free to destroy our data — walk-away territory. Redline repaired. |

## Walk-away items

These are the points our findings place in walk-away territory and we should treat as conditions of signature:

1. **No transition assistance or data return (Section 4(c)).** Kubient may simply destroy our data on termination. We need machine-readable return within 30 days plus certified deletion, with up to six months' assistance at then-current rates (90 days' assistance / 30-day export offered as the fallback).
2. **At-will revocability of the licence grant (paragraph 2).** Revocation is not tied to expiry or breach, so platform access could be pulled at will. Revocation must be limited to expiration or termination under paragraph 4.
3. **No insurance of any kind.** Kubient stores visitor data and holds our Confidential Information; total absence of coverage fails the fallback. We seek CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and workers' compensation as required by law, with certificates on request (fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
4. **90-day post-Initial-Term notice (RENEWAL).** At the outer edge of walk-away territory; we ask for 30 days, with 60 days as the fallback.

## Next steps

1. **Re-draft the two failed redlines before issuing comments.** The IP/data ownership clause and the licence-grant amendment did not pass verification. We will manually draft (i) an ownership clause confirming we retain all rights in our Content, Properties and Customer Data and own deliverables, with Kubient retaining its platform and background IP and granting a licence-back to embedded materials; and (ii) an amended paragraph 2 extending the grant to our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, confirming successor transferability, and limiting revocation to expiry or termination under paragraph 4.
2. **Issue the repaired redlines** on liability cap (mutual cap at the greater of amounts paid or payable in the preceding 12 months and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims and express confirmation that Kubient's revenue-share payment obligations are not capped damages), renewal notice, insurance (new General Provisions subsection (j)) and transition assistance (new Section 4(c)(v)–(vii)).
3. **Confirm the cap metric with the business.** Because Kubient pays us under Section 5, a cap keyed to "fees paid by Customer" would be illusory; we need sign-off on the paid-or-payable formulation and the USD 1,000,000 floor.
4. **Raise as drafting tidy-ups, if the negotiation is otherwise open:** the Delaware-law / New York-courts split and the tension between Section 8 (AAA arbitration) and Section 14(a) (exclusive court jurisdiction), which could invite a forum dispute.
5. **Hold the line on the four walk-away items above**; the balance of the Agreement is acceptable as drafted and we do not propose further redlines."}
